topic: Disorders of The Small and Large Intestine
stemEn: A child has abdominal pain and ultrasound shows the target sign of intussusception. Which listed condition is associated with this disease?
explanationAr: المصدر يطبع C كأكثر إجابة محتملة في الامتحانات، لكنه يذكر صراحة أن A (viral illness) يمكن أن تكون صحيحة أيضًا لأن adenovirus وURTI/gastroenteritis قد تترافق مع intussusception.
clinicalPearl: This source item is ambiguous: both HSP and preceding viral illness are recognized associations.

tts.text: A child has abdominal pain and ultrasound shows the target sign of intussusception. Which listed condition is associated with this disease? Option A. Viral illness. Option B. Meckel's diverticulum. Option C. Henoch-Schönlein purpura. Option D. Hirschsprung disease.

topic: Disorders of The Small and Large Intestine
stemEn: A 13-year-old girl has recurrent abdominal pain and vomiting for 3 months with 7-kg unintentional weight loss. Upper GI study shows a dilated stomach with abrupt duodenal cutoff. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanationAr: المصدر يختار Superior mesenteric artery syndrome ويشرح أن نقص mesenteric fat بعد weight loss قد يضيّق aortomesenteric angle ويضغط الجزء الثالث من duodenum.
clinicalPearl: Weight loss plus proximal duodenal dilation and abrupt cutoff suggests SMA syndrome.

What is the most likely diagnosis? Option A. Superior mesenteric artery syndrome. Option B. Peptic ulcer disease. Option C. GERD. Option D. Intussusception.

options.text: He is predisposed to have intestinal polyps
He is at risk to have thrombocytopenia

explanationAr: المصدر يختار predisposition to intestinal polyps ويشير إلى Peutz-Jeghers syndrome ذي النمط autosomal dominant.
clinicalPearl: PJS is inherited in an autosomal-dominant pattern and predisposes to GI hamartomatous polyps.

stemEn: A 10-year-old boy has intermittent bloody diarrhea with mucus for 3 months and weight loss. Which investigation should be requested?
explanationAr: المصدر يختار Colonoscopy with biopsy لتأكيد inflammatory bowel disease بعد استبعاد الأسباب المعدية حسب السياق.
clinicalPearl: Chronic bloody diarrhea with weight loss warrants endoscopic evaluation with tissue diagnosis.

stemEn: A child with ulcerative colitis on azathioprine develops abdominal pain, bloody diarrhea and fever. Labs show thrombocytosis, elevated ESR and CRP. What is the next step?

options.text: Stool culture and C. difficile toxin testing

explanationAr: المصدر يختار stool culture وC. difficile toxin testing، لكنه ينبه أن سؤالًا مشابهًا في مرجع آخر كان يضم abdominal X-ray كخيار مفضل. لذلك تُحفظ الإجابة المسترجعة منفصلة عن التحقق النهائي.
clinicalPearl: In a suspected UC flare, superimposed enteric infection—especially C. difficile—must be excluded.

stemEn: A child with inflammatory bowel disease started azathioprine 2 weeks ago and now has epigastric pain with elevated lipase and negative C. difficile testing. What should be done next?
explanationAr: المصدر يختار Stop azathioprine ويشرح أن pancreatitis من adverse effects المعروفة المبكرة لـazathioprine/6-MP.
clinicalPearl: New pancreatitis soon after azathioprine initiation should prompt withdrawal of the offending drug.

stemEn: A child with Crohn disease develops lower abdominal pain that is worsened by hip extension. What is the next step among the listed choices?
explanationAr: المصدر يختار Pelvic MRI من الخيارات، لكنه يذكر أن CT هو optimal imaging modality لتقييم psoas abscess لو كان موجودًا ضمن الخيارات.
clinicalPearl: Crohn disease plus pain on hip extension raises concern for psoas abscess.
